dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:3301.text: A particle marking the completion of an utterance. Formed from 矢, with 以 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3302.text: A short person. Formed from 矢, with 委 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3303.text: Lofty. Depicts the height of a terrace or lookout tower. Formed from 冂 and 口, on the same principle as 倉 and 舍. All characters in the 高 group follow 高.

shuowen:3304.text: A small hall. Formed from abbreviated 高, with 冋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3305.text: A place where people settle and rest. A 亭 has an upper story. Formed from abbreviated 高, with 丁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3306.text: A pavilion in Duling, Jingzhao. Formed from abbreviated 高, with 乇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3307.text: Outside a settlement is 郊; beyond 郊 is 野; beyond 野 is 林; beyond 林 is 冂. Depicts a distant boundary. All characters in the 冂 group follow 冂.

shuowen:3308.text: Where buying and selling take place. A market has enclosing walls. Formed from 冂 and 绁; 绁 is ancient-script 及, depicting goods reaching one another. Abbreviated 之 indicates the sound.

shuowen:3309.text: An unhurried manner of walking, 淫淫. Formed from 人 emerging from 冂.

shuowen:3310.text: The center. Formed from 大 inside 冂; 大 means a person. 央 and 㫄 use the same principle. Another explanation: long-lasting.

shuowen:3311.text: Reaching high. Formed from 隹 rising as if to emerge above 冂. The Changes says: “乾 is 隺然, lofty.”

shuowen:3312.text: A measured enclosure, where people measure out their dwelling places. Formed from 回, depicting the double walls of a city, with two towers facing each other. Some forms use only 囗. Pronounced 韋. All characters in this group follow 𩫖.

shuowen:3313.text: A gap. In antiquity the opening in a city wall on the south was called 𩫠. Formed from 𩫖 and abbreviated 缺. Read like 決 in the sense of pulling something out.

shuowen:3314.text: An exceptionally high mound made by people. Formed from abbreviated 高, with | depicting height. All characters in the 京 group follow 京.

shuowen:3315.text: 就 means high. Formed from 京 and 尤; 尤 means exceptional, beyond the ordinary.

shuowen:3316.text: To offer. Formed from abbreviated 高; 曰 depicts presenting cooked food. The Classic of Filial Piety says: “When sacrifices are offered, the spirits enjoy them.” All characters in this group follow 亯.

shuowen:3317.text: Cooked. Formed from 亯 and 羊. Read like 純. Another explanation: to boil.

shuowen:3318.text: Thick. Formed from 亯, with 竹 indicating the sound. Read like 篤.

shuowen:3319.text: To use. Formed from 亯 and 自; 自 recognizes the smell and fragrance of what is eaten. Read like 庸.

shuowen:3320.text: Thick. Formed from reversed 亯. All characters in the 𣆪 group follow 𣆪.

shuowen:3321.text: A lingering flavor. Formed from 𣆪, with abbreviated 鹹 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Truly far-reaching, truly great.”

shuowen:3322.text: The thickness of mountains and hills. Formed from 𣆪 and 厂.

shuowen:3323.text: Full. Formed from abbreviated 高, depicting height and thickness. All characters in this group follow 畗. Read like 伏.

shuowen:3324.text: Good. Formed from abbreviated 畗, with 亡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3325.text: Where grain is shaken in. For grain offerings in ancestral temples, one hurriedly takes grain from the granary; hence it is called 㐭. Formed from 入; 回 depicts a building with doors and windows inside. All characters in this group follow 㐭.

shuowen:3326.text: To grant grain. Formed from 㐭 and 禾.

shuowen:3327.text: Abundant grain. Formed from 㐭, with 旦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3328.text: Frugal or sparing. Formed from 口 and 㐭; 㐭 means receiving.

shuowen:3329.text: To cherish and conserve. Formed from 來 and 㐭: what comes is stored in a granary. Hence the agricultural official is called 嗇夫. All characters in this group follow 嗇.

shuowen:3330.text: An enclosing wall or screen. Formed from 嗇, with 爿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3331.text: The auspicious wheat, 來麰, received by Zhou. One 來 has two seams, depicting awns and spikes. It came from Heaven, so it also serves as 來 meaning “to come.” The Odes says: “They bequeathed us wheat and barley.” All characters in this group follow 來.

shuowen:3332.text: The Odes says: “Neither 𥏳 nor coming.” Formed from 來, with 矣 indicating the sound. The precise sense of 𥏳 here is uncertain.

shuowen:3333.text: An awned grain, planted in autumn and buried deeply, hence called 麥. Wheat belongs to Metal: it grows when Metal rules and dies when Fire rules. Formed from 來, the ear-bearing plant, and 夊. All characters in this group follow 麥.

shuowen:3334.text: 來麰, a cereal grain. Formed from 麥, with 牟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3335.text: Hard wheat grain. Formed from 麥, with 气 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3336.text: The hard particles in wheat bran. Formed from 麥, with 𧴪 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3337.text: To grind wheat. Formed from 麥, with 𢀩 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to pound.

shuowen:3338.text: The husks in wheat bran. Formed from 麥, with 夫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3339.text: Wheat flour. Formed from 麥, with 丏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3340.text: Crushed wheat kernels. Ten jin make three dou. Formed from 麥, with 啻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3341.text: Boiled wheat. Formed from 麥, with 豐 indicating the sound. Read like 馮.

shuowen:3342.text: Sweet wheat porridge. Formed from 麥, with 去 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3343.text: Fermentation cakes. Formed from 麥, with 㱿 indicating the sound. Read like 庫.

shuowen:3344.text: Fermentation cakes. Formed from 麥, with 穴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3345.text: Fermentation cakes. Formed from 麥, with 才 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3346.text: To walk slowly, dragging the feet, 夊夊. Depicts a person whose two shins tread upon something. All characters in this group follow 夊.

shuowen:3347.text: A 夋夋 manner of walking. Another explanation: arrogant. Formed from 夊, with 允 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3348.text: To follow an old path. Formed from 夊, with abbreviated 畗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3349.text: To pass beyond. Formed from 夊 and 𡴆; 𡴆 means high. Another explanation: 夌约, constriction; this phrase is uncertain.

shuowen:3350.text: To send or escort to a destination. Formed from 夊 and 至.

shuowen:3351.text: A harmonious manner of proceeding. Formed from 夊, with 𢚧 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “He spreads government harmoniously.”

shuowen:3352.text: A manner of walking. Formed from 夊, with 㤅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3353.text: A 𡰿𡰿 manner of walking. Formed from 夊; the remaining analysis is missing. Read like 僕.

shuowen:3354.text: To sing and dance. Music has patterned sections. Formed from 章, 夅 and 夊. The Odes says: “Dance for me, 竷竷.”

shuowen:3355.text: The covering of the brain. Depicts skin enclosing the brain, with two arms below and 夊 beneath them. Read like 范.

shuowen:3356.text: The people of the central states. Formed from 夊, 頁 and 𦥑; 𦥑 represents two hands and 夊 two feet.

shuowen:3357.text: Advancing steadily in cultivating crops, 畟畟. Formed from 田, 人 and 夊. The Odes says: “Steadily advance the good plowshares.”

shuowen:3358.text: To draw in the feet. Birds of the magpie and shrike kind draw in their feet when flying. Formed from 夊, with 兇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3359.text: A greedy beast. Another explanation: a monkey, resembling a person. Formed from 頁, with 巳, 止 and 夊 representing its hands and feet.

shuowen:3360.text: A divine spirit. Like a dragon, with one foot: formed from 夊, depicting horns, hands and a human face.

shuowen:3361.text: To lose proper bearing when bowing. Formed from 夊, with 坐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3362.text: To lie facing opposite ways. Formed from 夊 and 𡕒 with their backs to each other. All characters in this group follow 舛.

shuowen:3363.text: Dance or music. Uses feet facing opposite ways, hence 舛; 無 indicates the sound.

shuowen:3364.text: The retaining pin at the end of a cart axle. Two holes face opposite ways, hence 舛; abbreviated 𥜿 indicates the sound. 𥜿 is ancient-script 偰.

shuowen:3365.text: A plant called 葍 in Chu and 藑 in Qin. It trails along the ground with connected flowers. Pictographic, formed from 舛, which also indicates the sound. All characters in the 䑞 group follow 䑞. In modern clerical transformation it is written 舜.

shuowen:3366.text: Flowers flourishing. Formed from 舜, with 生 indicating the sound. Read like 皇. The Erya says: “𤰀 means flower.”

shuowen:3367.text: To turn away from one another. Formed from 舛, with 囗 indicating the sound. Animal hide can bind things that bend and turn away from one another; hence the graph is borrowed for leather. All characters in this group follow 韋.

shuowen:3368.text: A ceremonial apron, 韍, covering the front and made of leather. Two chi wide below, one chi above, with a neck five cun wide. At the first investiture, a dark red apron; at the second, a red apron. Formed from 韋, with 畢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3369.text: Leather dyed with madder. One immersion in dye is called 韎. Formed from 韋, with 末 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3370.text: The fastening of a case. Formed from 韋, with 惠 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a sack for holding captives’ heads.

shuowen:3371.text: A sword sheath. Formed from 韋, with 舀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3372.text: An archer’s arm guard. Formed from 韋, with 冓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3373.text: An archer’s thumb ring, used to hold the bowstring; made of ivory or bone, tied with leather and worn on the right thumb. Formed from 韋, with 枼 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The boy wears a thumb ring.”

shuowen:3374.text: A bow case. Formed from 韋, with 蜀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3375.text: A bow case. Formed from 韋, with 長 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Two bows in crossed cases.”

shuowen:3376.text: Footwear. Formed from 韋, with 叚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3377.text: The patch at the back of a shoe. Formed from 韋, with 段 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3378.text: A covering for the foot. Formed from 韋, with 蔑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3379.text: A covering for a yoke. Formed from 韋, with 尃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3380.text: Leather divided through the middle is called 韏. Formed from 韋, with 𢍏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3381.text: To gather and bind. Formed from 韋, with 𥼚 indicating the sound. Read like 酋.

shuowen:3382.text: A well enclosure. Formed from 韋, taking its sense of surrounding, with 倝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3383.text: Supple yet strong. Formed from 韋, with 刃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3384.text: The successive turns of a leather binding. Based on the shape of an ancient graph. All characters in this group follow 弟.

shuowen:3385.text: The Zhou people call an elder brother 𥊽. Formed from 弟 and 𥄳.

shuowen:3386.text: To arrive from behind. Depicts someone propelling a person from behind the two shins. All characters in this group follow 夂. Read like 黹.

shuowen:3387.text: To intercept one another at a vital point. Formed from 夂, with 丯 indicating the sound. Xinye in Nanyang has a 𡕗 Pavilion.

shuowen:3388.text: To oppose or encounter. Formed from 夂, with 𡴀 indicating the sound. Read like 縫.

shuowen:3389.text: To submit. Formed from 夂 and 午, one following the other, not daring to stand side by side.

shuowen:3390.text: In Qin, getting extra in a market purchase is called 夃. Formed from 𠄎 and 夂, meaning an increase arriving; it uses 乃. The Odes says: “Let me pour from that bronze wine jar.”

shuowen:3391.text: To take a stride. Formed from reversed 夂. 𩰫 follows this element.

shuowen:3392.text: To brace from behind. Depicts a support behind a person’s two shins. The Rites of Zhou says: “Brace them against a wall to observe their bending.” All characters in this group follow 久.

shuowen:3393.text: To dismember and expose. Formed from 舛 upon 木. All characters in this group follow 桀.

shuowen:3394.text: To dismember as punishment. Formed from 桀, with 石 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3395.text: To cover. Formed from 入 and 桀; 桀 means cunning. In military regulations it is called 乘. The connection is uncertain.

shuowen:3396.text: To emerge: growing up through the ground. The phase of the east. Formed from 屮, with roots depicted below. All characters in this group follow 木.

shuowen:3397.text: A fruit from south of the Yangtze. Formed from 木, with 矞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3398.text: A kind of mandarin orange. Formed from 木, with 登 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3399.text: The 條 fruit, resembling an orange but sour. Formed from 木, with 由 indicating the sound. The Book of Xia says: “Their wrapped offerings were mandarins and pomelos.”

shuowen:3400.text: A fruit resembling a pear but sour. Formed from 木, with 虘 indicating the sound.
